title: Design System: Open Voice — El Núcleo Vivo

transcribing.note: The microphone's colour and the capturing phase. 5.24:1 on ground, 4.37:1 on panel — check the surface under it.

thinking.note: Model streaming, no audio yet. Also the active-entry border and the focus outline.

speaking.note: Synthesized audio playing. The warmest and quietest code in the set.

idle.note: Nothing is happening. Desaturated so idleness reads as absence of signal.

cut.note: Reserved for an interruption and for the states where a stream is open. Never decoration.

display.purpose: The product name, once, in the header, at 2.25rem/36px. Never reused as a section heading.

readout.purpose: The current entry's FAC number at 2.5rem/40px. The world's real headline.

body.purpose: Document default, the header subtitle, and the composer text input, at 0.9375rem/15px. Lives on body, never on html, so the rem base stays 16px.

label.purpose: Uppercase system caps at 0.8125rem/13px: language mark, column heading, panel headings.

caption.purpose: Instrumentation terms and panel status text at 0.6875rem/11px. Read, not engraved — never uppercase.

preview.purpose: The truncated entry preview in the index.

composer-control.purpose: Mono, uppercase, 0.08em tracking, 0.6875rem/11px. Every composer button label.

mono-number.purpose: Every latency value and the FAC column, with tabular figures so columns align.

shadows.name: field-bar-glow
shadows.purpose: Canvas glow on each spectral bar, scaled by the FFT magnitude it measures. Glow lives in the canvas field alone — the CSS chrome carries no shadows.

shadows.name: core-halo
shadows.purpose: Canvas glow on the living core's 25%-alpha halo pass.

motion.name: ease-signal
motion.purpose: Composer controls: 160ms on border-color and color. A signal settling, not a bounce.

motion.name: ease-surface
motion.purpose: 200ms on background-color and color for hover fills in the turn index.

motion.name: plot-signal
motion.purpose: The field samples real spectrum every 16ms and draws every frame. The sweep advances by 0.006 + level * 0.05 radians per frame, so the motion encodes amplitude rather than a constant rotation.

motion.name: spectrum-fold
motion.purpose: The analyser's dB bins fold into 72 bars on a log-ish spread — more resolution where the voice lives — and each bar peak-holds with a decay, so speech rises fast and falls smoothly.

motion.name: motion-off
motion.purpose: Stops the animation after one frame. The field rests; the guide rings remain.

components.name: Send Button
components.description: The composer submit control. The only filled-inverted button in the system; on hover it loses the fill rather than brightening.
components.css: .ds-btn-submit { background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); color: #000000; border: 1px solid hsl(0, 0%, 20%); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.5rem 0.875rem; font-family: 'Azeret Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 200ms ease; } .ds-btn-submit:hover:not(:disabled), .ds-btn-submit:focus-visible:not(:disabled) { background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 10%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); } .ds-btn-submit:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid hsl(50, 80%, 50%); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-submit:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Resting state for Live-off, Stop, and Reconnect now. One tonal step on hover, never a shadow.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 10%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); border: 1px solid hsl(0, 0%, 20%); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.5rem 0.875rem; font-family: 'Azeret Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 200ms ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover:not(:disabled), .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible:not(:disabled) { background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 15%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid hsl(50, 80%, 50%); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Live Button (open stream)
components.description: Red while a stream is open. Hover steps the red down, never up. Disabled while a turn is in flight so toggling it can never cut an active request.
components.css: .ds-btn-live-on { background-color: hsl(0, 80%, 50%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); border: 1px solid hsl(0, 0%, 20%); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.5rem 0.875rem; font-family: 'Azeret Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 200ms ease; } .ds-btn-live-on:hover:not(:disabled), .ds-btn-live-on:focus-visible:not(:disabled) { background-color: hsl(0, 80%, 40%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); } .ds-btn-live-on:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid hsl(50, 80%, 50%); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-live-on:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Recording Button
components.description: Push-to-talk while the button is held. Visually identical to Live: red means audio is being captured, whichever control opened it.
components.css: .ds-btn-recording { background-color: hsl(0, 80%, 50%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); border: 1px solid hsl(0, 0%, 20%); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.5rem 0.875rem; font-family: 'Azeret Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 200ms ease; } .ds-btn-recording:hover:not(:disabled), .ds-btn-recording:focus-visible:not(:disabled) { background-color: hsl(0, 80%, 40%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); } .ds-btn-recording:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid hsl(50, 80%, 50%); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-recording:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Mic Switch
components.description: The explicit microphone gate, role=switch with aria-checked. Signal Blue when armed — the microphone's colour, never red. Off means the microphone is closed: capture stops immediately and the in-flight turn finalizes with the audio already captured.
components.css: .ds-mic-switch { background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 10%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); border: 1px solid hsl(0, 0%, 20%); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.5rem 0.875rem; font-family: 'Azeret Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 200ms ease; } .ds-mic-switch[aria-checked="true"] { background-color: hsl(210, 80%, 50%); border-color: hsl(210, 80%, 50%); color: #000000; } .ds-mic-switch[aria-checked="true"]:hover, .ds-mic-switch[aria-checked="true"]:focus-visible { background-color: hsl(210, 80%, 50%); border-color: hsl(0, 0%, 80%); color: #000000; } .ds-mic-switch:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid hsl(50, 80%, 50%); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Message Field
components.description: The required text path. Square, on the panel ground, with the selection and caret pulled into the palette.
components.css: .ds-input { background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 10%); color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); border: 1px solid hsl(0, 0%, 20%); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; min-width: 120px; font-family: Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; line-height: 1.5; caret-color: hsl(0, 0%, 95%); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: hsl(0, 0%, 70%); } .ds-input::selection { background-color: hsl(210, 80%, 50%); color: #000000; }

components.name: Catalog Entry
components.description: One numbered turn in the left index. Marked by a left border when active, and struck permanently when cut.
components.css: .ds-nav-entry { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2.75rem 1fr; align-items: baseline; gap: 0.5rem; width: 100%; padding: 0.375rem 0.5rem; text-align: left; background: transparent; border: 0; border-left: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0; color: hsl(0, 0%, 70%); font-family: Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; cursor: pointer; transition: color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-nav-entry:hover { color: hsl(0, 0%, 80%); background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 15%); } .ds-nav-entry:focus-visible { color: hsl(0, 0%, 80%); background-color: hsl(0, 0%, 15%); outline: 1px solid hsl(50, 80%, 50%); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-nav-fac { font-family: 'Azeret Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 400; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-nav-preview { font-size: 0.75rem; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-nav-active { color: hsl(0, 0%, 80%); border-left-color: hsl(50, 80%, 50%); } .ds-nav-cut .ds-nav-preview { text-decoration: line-through; text-decoration-color: hsl(0, 80%, 50%); text-decoration-thickness: 1px; } .ds-nav-cut .ds-nav-fac { color: hsl(0, 80%, 50%); }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Connection state, engraved and square. Colour does the work; the word confirms it.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 96px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; background: transparent; border: 1px solid hsl(210, 80%, 50%); border-radius: 0; color: hsl(210, 80%, 50%); font-family: Archivo, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: The Living Core
components.description: The signature component: the agent's presence as a spectral field — 72 bars around a breathing core with a radar sweep, all driven by real FFT data. This snapshot is the speaking phase, where the ring owns the full spectrum. Use the live app to see it move.
components.css: .ds-field { position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; background-color: #000000; overflow: hidden; } .ds-field svg { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; }

narrative.overview:
The interface is a dark room with one living presence: a radial field at the center of the screen that breathes with the amplitude of the conversation. The world is a speaking agent seen as energy. When the user talks, seventy-two spectral bars ignite around a glowing core; when the agent answers, the whole ring turns through the visible spectrum. Everything else stays quiet — matte black ground, dark panels, one-pixel hairlines, and a compact type scale that fits a working session on a single screen.

The chrome is deliberately flat so the field owns the eye. No corner is rounded, no surface casts a shadow, no panel is translucent. Depth in the interface is a two-step tonal floor between black and a very dark gray, and all glow lives in the canvas alone. The design is dense rather than explanatory: the user already knows the product, and the interface's job is to prove what just happened, measured.

The conversation itself is a catalog of numbered turns. Every entry carries a zero-padded FAC number in tabular monospace, an answer is the entry under the current number — never a chat bubble — and an interrupted turn is struck through in red for the life of the session. Latency is a feature: per-turn timings and the live voice-activity readout sit permanently in the right rail, because the measurements are the authority over intuition. The microphone is never ambient: it opens only when the user arms it, through the Mic switch, push-to-talk, or Live mode.
keyCharacteristics: A living radial field: 72 spectral bars, a breathing core, and a radar sweep, all driven by real FFT data from the microphone and the reply playback
The speaking phase owns the full visible spectrum — the world's one deliberate multi-hue moment
Matte black ground, panel void, one-pixel hairlines; glow lives in the canvas alone
Zero corner radius on every control, panel, strip and readout
Engraved tracked capitals for system words; tabular monospace for every number
Compact density: the whole working session fits one screen above 1024px

rules.name: The Phase Code Rule
rules.body: Every product phase owns exactly one colour — idle steel, transcribing blue, thinking amber, speaking bone — and the colour strip in the right rail is the only place a phase appears as a large flat fill. A cut is never a phase on the strip: interruption lives as the permanent red strike in the turn index, where it stays for the life of the session.

rules.name: The Spectrum Rule
rules.body: The speaking field is the world's one deliberate full-spectrum moment. While the agent speaks, each of the 72 bars takes a hue from a band drifting with the sweep — hsl((index × 3.5 + sweepAngle × 24) mod 360, 85%, 52–68%) — so a reply is visibly a wave of colour moving through the ring. Every other phase keeps its single hue, and no other element in the interface uses more than one.

rules.name: The Glow Belongs To The Field Rule
rules.body: All glow is canvas glow: spectral bars cast a shadowBlur of 8 + magnitude×16 in their own colour, and the core casts 26. The CSS chrome carries no box-shadow, no blur, and no translucency — depth there is the two-tone ground and one-pixel hairlines.

rules.name: The Flat-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Hover adds exactly one step (panel void → hsl(0, 0%, 15%)), a 1.15:1 lift visible as a change of surface, not a glow. If a new surface needs to read as raised, add a tone or a hairline — never a shadow.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two ground values in the interface: #000000 for the field and the shell, hsl(0, 0%, 10%) for panels. A third background tone is a new design decision, not an implementation detail.

rules.name: The Engraved Rule
rules.body: System text is uppercase with wide tracking (0.05em for Archivo labels, 0.08em for monospace control labels). Sentence case is reserved for content that came from speech or from the user.

rules.name: The Numbering Rule
rules.body: Every number is set in Azeret Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, and FAC numbers are zero-padded to three digits (007, not 7) so the column does not reflow as the catalog grows. Never style a numeral in the display face.

dos: Do drive the field from real FFT data only — microphone and playback analysers — and let a bar rest when its magnitude falls below 0.012.
Do let the speaking phase own the full spectrum, and keep every other phase in its single hue.
Do keep the chrome flat: two ground tones, one-pixel hairlines, zero radius, and glow only in the canvas.
Do set every number in Azeret Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, zero-padded to three digits for FAC numbers.
Do write system text in engraved tracked caps, and reserve sentence case for words the user or the agent said.
Do show an em dash for an unmeasured value instead of a zero or a spinner.
Do keep the Mic switch in Signal Blue — the microphone's colour — and Cut Red for streaming and cut states.
Do arm the playback graph on every gesture that can begin a turn, so the first reply never waits on the browser's autoplay policy.
donts: Don't add corner radius to anything; the only rounded element in the system is the browser's scrollbar thumb.
Don't put a box-shadow, blur, gradient, or translucent surface in the CSS chrome — glow belongs to the field alone.
Don't render the conversation as chat bubbles, or the microphone as a round button. An answer is the entry under the current FAC number.
Don't use the Cut Red token for anything but an interruption or an open stream — not errors in general, not hover, not emphasis.
Don't animate the bars from a random walk or a constant waveform; the sweep's baseline turn is modulated by signal, and bars rest without it.
Don't take a system face for the display voice or the numerals. Both faces are self-hosted woff2 files, and the numerals must stay tabular in every readout.
Don't translate. The language mark names the answering voice; the product does not translate.
Don't fetch fonts at runtime, and don't imply a capability the backend lacks — the interface shows only the states the product can actually produce.
